acceptance_criteria: AC-1 decide_start returns resume for a failed record whose failure reasons are exactly {budget_exhausted}.
AC-2 decide_start returns dispatch, not resume, for a failed record whose failure reasons contain budget_exhausted together with at least one other reason. A test asserts this explicitly.
AC-3 decide_start returns dispatch for every other terminal record, unchanged.
AC-4 A budget resume with a ceiling less than or equal to the stopping ceiling is refused, and the refusal reason names both numbers.
AC-5 A budget resume reuses worktree_path, branch and session id, creates no new worktree and consumes no new worker slot.
AC-6 retry_count increments on a budget resume, and a record at retry_limit is not resumable by this path.
AC-7 The run report of a resumed run identifies it as a budget resume and records the ceiling it was given.
AC-8 python3 -m pytest tests/test_orchestrator.py -q passes with at least three new tests, covering AC-1, AC-2 and AC-4.
AC-9 The repository privacy gate reports zero findings.
AC-10 The diff touches scripts/orchestrator.py and tests/test_orchestrator.py and nothing else.

baseline.current_behaviour: scripts/orchestrator.py: decide_start reaches its resume branch only when the existing record's phase is not in TERMINAL_PHASES, and TERMINAL_PHASES contains PHASE_FAILED. Budget exhaustion is already detected and recorded -- the run report carries a budget_exhausted object with max_budget_usd and cost_reached_usd, and failure_reasons carries the string budget_exhausted alongside any other reasons. Those recorded values are the input this movement needs; it does not need to detect anything new.

retry_count and retry_limit semantics are unchanged.

report.objective: Make a budget-exhausted movement resumable, exactly as docs/design/GOV_ORCH_10_BUDGET_EXHAUSTION_IS_RESUMABLE.md (FROZEN 2026-09-13) decides it: decide_start returns resume for a record that failed for that reason and no other, a resume must be given a higher ceiling than the one that stopped it, and everything else about budgets, retries and terminal phases stays exactly as it is.
output_contract: A resume path that a Product Owner assistant can use by raising the ceiling and re-running, with no new worktree and no lost session context.
A mixed-reason test that proves the amendment did not make every failure resumable.
SESSION_CLOSE naming which of R-1 to R-6 has code, which acceptance item each new test covers, and the tests/test_orchestrator.py count before and after.

recommended_reasoning.reason: Small diff, but it changes a safety classification in the dispatch loop: the difference between 'ran out of money' and 'produced something wrong' is the entire content of the change, and getting it loose would let a failed movement restart as if it were merely interrupted. High effort for the care, not for the volume.

requirements: English, per AGENTS.md engineering-output language law.
Read GOV.ORCH.10 fully first. Every rule you implement must be traceable to one of R-1 to R-6, and each new test names the acceptance item it covers.

Do not introduce a second notion of 'budget failure'. The recorded failure_reasons list is the single signal; if the record does not persist enough to decide R-2, persist it rather than re-deriving it from a log.
Commit early and often on the lane: the decide_start change, the ceiling refusal, the report field, and the tests as separate commits.
Do not merge to main. The Product Owner assistant reviews the diff and merges.

Do not run the full pytest suite. It creates untracked data/ and logs/ directories that the repository privacy gate then flags, which fails a movement whose diff is clean. tests/test_orchestrator.py is the suite that matters here.
If GOV.ORCH.10 does not answer something, raise one RELAY_QUESTION rather than deciding it.
risks: Making every failed record resumable, which would let a movement that failed verification be restarted as though it had merely run out of money. R-2 and AC-2 exist for this.
Writing a second resume path instead of reusing the one that already reuses worktree, branch and session.
Deciding R-2 from a log tail rather than from the persisted failure reasons, which would make the decision non-deterministic.
Allowing a resume into the same or a lower ceiling, which burns the resumed session's start-up cost and stops in the same place.
Quietly changing retry_limit or TERMINAL_PHASES for unrelated phases.
Touching the state records of the already-merged movements to demonstrate the feature.

in: In scripts/orchestrator.py, allow decide_start to return resume for an existing record whose phase is failed when its recorded failure reasons contain budget_exhausted AND contain nothing else (GOV.ORCH.10 R-1, R-2). Every other terminal record, and every budget-exhausted record that carries any additional failure reason, keeps returning dispatch exactly as today.

Refuse a resume under R-1 when the new --max-budget-usd is less than or equal to the ceiling that stopped the movement, and state both numbers in the refusal reason (R-3). The stopping ceiling is available from the persisted record or its report; read it rather than asking the caller to restate it.

A resume under R-1 must go through the SAME resume path that already exists: reuse the recorded worktree_path, branch and engineer session id, create no new worktree, and consume no new worker slot (R-1 and acceptance item 4). Do not write a second resume implementation.
retry_count increments on a budget resume exactly as it already does on every resume, and a record at retry_limit is not resumable by this path either (R-4, acceptance item 5).
The run report of a resumed run records that it was a budget resume and the ceiling it was given (acceptance item 6). Add the minimum field that carries this; do not restructure the report.

Tests in tests/test_orchestrator.py for acceptance items 1, 2 and 3, with item 2 covering at least one explicit MIXED-reason case -- a record whose failure reasons contain budget_exhausted together with another reason, asserted to return dispatch and NOT resume. That mixed case is the whole safety of the amendment and a test that omits it proves nothing.

Keep decide_start a pure function of its arguments, as its own docstring says it is. If it needs the failure reasons, they arrive through the existing record argument, not through a new read inside it.
out: Changing DEFAULT_MAX_BUDGET_USD, or its value anywhere.
Letting a worker raise or influence its own ceiling by any path.
Automatic or implicit resume. A resume happens only because a caller explicitly ran the command with a higher ceiling.
Making any other failure reason resumable. budget_exhausted alone, and only alone.
Changing retry_limit, TERMINAL_PHASES membership for any other purpose, reconcile_phase's meaning, verification, the relay protocol, or the report schema beyond acceptance item 6.
Editing docs/design/GOV_ORCH_1_*.md or any other FROZEN contract.
Any change under ui2/, utils/, application/ or project/.
Retro-fitting this to the already-closed movements NXS-LOCAL-0130 or NXS-LOCAL-0131. Their work is merged; do not touch their state records.

recommended_reasoning.reason: Matches the SESSION_START recommendation: small diff, but the change is a safety classification in the dispatch loop (interrupted-by-limit vs. produced-something-wrong), so review warrants the same care as implementation.

unresolved_risks: Under the current _cmd_run construction, adapter.budget_exhausted(log_path) is only ever consulted inside the 'if exit_code != 0:' branch, after 'engineer_exit_nonzero' has already been appended to failure_reasons -- so a real `run` invocation's failure_reasons for a budget-exhausted engineer is today always at least ['engineer_exit_nonzero', 'budget_exhausted'], never budget_exhausted alone (confirmed by the pre-existing test_run_cli_budget_exhausted_names_its_own_failure_reason fixture). This movement's scope was decide_start's decision logic, the ceiling refusal, resume-path reuse, retry accounting and the report field -- not the failure_reasons construction rule in _cmd_run -- so R-1/R-2 are implemented and tested exactly as GOV.ORCH.10 section 4 items 1-3 specify (against directly-constructed records), but whether an unmodified `run` invocation can ever naturally produce a record this new path acts on was left open rather than decided or silently fixed. Recommend a follow-up movement to decide whether engineer_exit_nonzero should be withheld when the non-zero exit is explained by budget_exhausted.
